title: Clementine: the last Goldkette head arrangement
summary: Doc Ryker pushed the band to work up Clementine at the final Victor date, with a strong Bix chorus.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: So that was my next move, anyway. But the band, in the meantime, as I understand it, they left here and went to Roseland and that's where they made "Clementine," at that particular time. I contributed another arrangement that I did for them. That was strictly a head arrangement. If anybody should have should be Doc Ryker, credit for it, it was Doc Reiker, who used to take the band is conduct and where they were going and what they were going to do very seriously. He was afraid it would break up. He was afraid the band wouldn't go on. He had been in it since its beginning and he didn't want to see anything happen to it if it could be avoided.

So he would be around and he would, I guess he took the orchestration and told Trumbauer to get his saxophone thing, work out a saxophone chorus and then it would give -- well, Bix didn't have -- tell them to woodshed, we had a term then go over in your corner and woodshed these parts and then we'd come back and put the whole thing together.
